newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy meetings over budget going very well - Prodi.
newsitem.headline: Italy meetings over budget going very well - Prodi.

text.p: Talks between the government, unions and employers on the impact of the 1997 budget on workers were going well and would continue on Tuesday, Prime Minister Romano Prodi said.
Prodi told reporters after more than five hours of talks that they were "proceeding in an extremely positive way."
Prodi's comments appeared to indicate the possibility of a general strike over union concerns about the impact of the cost-cutting budget had been averted for the time being.

Prodi also said Labour Minister Tiziano Treu will call a special meeting between metalworkers threatening more strike action and their employers federation if talks over a new contract did not reach a breakthrough within 10 days.

Leaders of the powerful three main union confederations were seeking clarification of a proposed "Euro-tax" designed to raise 12.5 trillion lire and help Italy qualify at the outset for a European single currency.
Prodi said a concluding news conference would be held on Tuesday after the end of the talks to release and explain the precise figures and the make-up of the provision.

The budget, which aims to strip 62.5 trillion lire ($41 billion) from next year's projected public sector deficit, was passed by the Chamber of Deputies (lower house) over the weekend, but union leaders remain opposed to some parts.
Union leaders are concerned that measures to stimulate job creation are missing from the draft budget. They also want progress on renewing contracts for metalworkers that lapsed in June.
Metalworkers unions have scheduled a strike on November 22 to press demands for a new contract. The strike would be their second in two months.
Prodi was joined for the talks by Deputy Prime Minister Walter Veltroni, Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi, Treu and Finance Minister Vincenzo Visco.
